questions.prompt: Solve for x: 2(x − 3) + 4 = 3x − 7
questions.workedSolution: Expand the brackets: 2x − 6 + 4 = 3x − 7, so 2x − 2 = 3x − 7. Subtract 2x from both sides: −2 = x − 7. Add 7 to both sides: x = 5. Check: 2(5 − 3) + 4 = 4 + 4 = 8 and 3(5) − 7 = 15 − 7 = 8, so the solution x = 5 is consistent.

questions.prompt: Find the sum of the squares of the roots of x² − 7x + 12 = 0
questions.workedSolution: Factorise: (x − 3)(x − 4) = 0, so the roots are x = 3 and x = 4. Their squares are 9 and 16, giving a sum of 25. Cross-check with root relations: sum of roots = 7 and product = 12, so sum of squares = 7² − 2(12) = 49 − 24 = 25.

provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Core Mathematics

questions.prompt: A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Using π = 22/7, calculate its volume.
questions.workedSolution: Volume of a cylinder V = πr²h. Substitute r = 7 cm and h = 10 cm: V = (22/7) × 7² × 10 = (22/7) × 49 × 10 = 22 × 7 × 10 = 1540 cm³. The 7 in the denominator cancels with the 49 from r², which is why 22/7 is a convenient approximation here.

questions.prompt: A bag contains 3 red and 2 blue balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.workedSolution: P(first red) = 3/5. After removing one red ball, 2 red remain out of 4 balls, so P(second red | first red) = 2/4 = 1/2. Multiply because the draws are dependent: P(both red) = 3/5 × 1/2 = 3/10 = 0.3.

questions.prompt: Evaluate log base 10 of 1000.
questions.workedSolution: Since 1000 = 10³, log₁₀ 1000 = 3 by the definition of a logarithm as the power to which the base must be raised.

questions.prompt: What is the derivative of x³ with respect to x?
questions.workedSolution: By the power rule d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹ with n = 3, the derivative is 3x². This gives the gradient of the cubic curve at any point x.

questions.prompt: What is the exact value of cos 60°?
questions.workedSolution: From the standard 30-60-90 triangle, cos 60° = adjacent/hypotenuse = 1/2. It is one of the exact trigonometric values expected to be recalled instantly.

questions.prompt: What is the next term of the sequence 2, 5, 8, 11, …?
questions.workedSolution: Each term increases by a common difference of 3, so the sequence is arithmetic. The next term is 11 + 3 = 14.

questions.prompt: If 3x − 7 = 11, what is the value of x?
questions.workedSolution: Add 7 to both sides: 3x = 18. Divide both sides by 3: x = 6. Substitution confirms it: 3(6) − 7 = 18 − 7 = 11.

questions.workedSolution: When multiplying powers with the same base, add the indices: 2³ × 2⁴ = 2⁷ = 128. A common error is multiplying the bases or the indices, giving wrong values such as 4¹².

questions.prompt: What is the size of each exterior angle of a regular octagon?
questions.workedSolution: The exterior angles of any convex polygon sum to 360°. A regular octagon has 8 equal exterior angles, so each is 360° ÷ 8 = 45°. (Each interior angle is then 180° − 45° = 135°.)

questions.prompt: If tan θ = 1 and θ is acute, what is the value of θ?
questions.workedSolution: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ = 1 means sin θ = cos θ, which for an acute angle occurs only at θ = 45°. At 90° tangent is undefined, and at 30° and 60° it equals 1/√3 and √3 respectively.

questions.prompt: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 4 m/s² for 5 s. How far does it travel?
questions.workedSolution: Use s = ut + ½at² with u = 0, a = 4 m/s² and t = 5 s: s = 0 + ½ × 4 × 5² = 2 × 25 = 50 m. The final speed would be v = u + at = 20 m/s, but the question asks only for distance.

provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Physics

questions.prompt: A 12 V battery is connected across a 4 Ω and an 8 Ω resistor in series. Calculate the power dissipated in the 8 Ω resistor.
questions.workedSolution: Series resistances add: R = 4 + 8 = 12 Ω. Circuit current I = V/R = 12/12 = 1 A, and the same current flows through each resistor in series. Power in the 8 Ω resistor: P = I²R = 1² × 8 = 8 W.

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana
provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Physics

questions.prompt: Calculate the heat required to raise the temperature of 0.5 kg of water from 20 °C to 70 °C. (c = 4200 J/kg°C)
questions.workedSolution: Q = mcΔT with m = 0.5 kg, c = 4200 J/kg°C and ΔT = 70 − 20 = 50 °C: Q = 0.5 × 4200 × 50 = 105 000 J = 105 kJ. Note the temperature change is used, not the final temperature.

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana
provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Physics

questions.prompt: A wave covers 340 m in 2.0 s. If its frequency is 85 Hz, what is its wavelength?
questions.workedSolution: First find the speed: v = distance/time = 340/2.0 = 170 m/s. Then apply the wave equation v = fλ, so λ = v/f = 170/85 = 2.0 m. Two steps are required: speed from kinematics, then wavelength from the wave relation.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of energy?
questions.workedSolution: The joule (J) is the SI unit of energy and work; 1 J = 1 N·m = 1 kg·m²/s². It is named after James Prescott Joule.

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana
provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Physics

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of electrical power?
questions.workedSolution: The watt (W) is the SI unit of power, equal to one joule per second. In circuits P = IV = I²R = V²/R, all giving watts.

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana
provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Physics

questions.prompt: What is the bending of light as it passes from air into water called?
questions.workedSolution: Refraction is the change in direction of a wave when its speed changes at a boundary between media. Snell’s law, n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂, quantifies it.

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana
provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Physics

questions.prompt: Which particle is emitted from a nucleus during beta-minus decay?
questions.workedSolution: In beta-minus decay a neutron converts to a proton and emits an electron (the beta particle) plus an antineutrino. The atomic number rises by one while the mass number is unchanged.

questions.prompt: Which of the following quantities is a vector?
questions.workedSolution: A vector has both magnitude and direction. Velocity includes direction, unlike speed (its magnitude), mass and temperature, which are scalars. Other common vectors are force, acceleration and displacement.

questions.workedSolution: In the visible spectrum, red light has the longest wavelength (about 700 nm) and violet the shortest (about 400 nm). Frequency runs the opposite way because v = fλ for a fixed speed of light.

questions.prompt: Calculate the number of moles in 20.0 g of sodium hydroxide, NaOH. (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
questions.workedSolution: Molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g/mol. Moles n = mass/molar mass = 20.0/40 = 0.5 mol. This is the standard n = m/M relationship used throughout quantitative chemistry.

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana
provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Chemistry

questions.prompt: What volume does 0.25 mol of an ideal gas occupy at s.t.p.? (Molar volume = 22.4 dm³/mol)
questions.workedSolution: Volume = moles × molar volume = 0.25 × 22.4 = 5.6 dm³. At standard temperature and pressure one mole of any ideal gas occupies 22.4 dm³, so a quarter mole occupies a quarter of that volume.

questions.prompt: A current of 2.0 A is passed through a solution of AgNO₃ for 965 s. Calculate the mass of silver deposited. (F = 96 500 C/mol, Ag = 108 g/mol)
questions.workedSolution: Charge Q = It = 2.0 × 965 = 1930 C. Moles of electrons = Q/F = 1930/96 500 = 0.02 mol. The half-equation Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag shows one electron deposits one silver atom, so n(Ag) = 0.02 mol. Mass = 0.02 × 108 = 2.16 g.

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana
provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Chemistry

questions.prompt: For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) at equilibrium, [N₂] = 0.10 M, [H₂] = 0.10 M and [NH₃] = 0.20 M. Calculate the value of Kc.
questions.workedSolution: Kc = [NH₃]²/([N₂][H₂]³) using the stoichiometric coefficients as powers. Substituting: Kc = (0.20)²/(0.10 × (0.10)³) = 0.04/0.0001 = 400. The units are (mol dm⁻³)²/(mol dm⁻³)⁴ = mol⁻² dm⁶.

questions.prompt: How many protons are in the nucleus of a carbon atom?
questions.workedSolution: The atomic number Z counts the protons in the nucleus. Carbon has 6 protons, so Z = 6; this fixes its position in group 14 of the periodic table.

questions.prompt: What type of bond holds the atoms together within a water molecule?
questions.workedSolution: Within H₂O, hydrogen and oxygen share electron pairs, forming covalent bonds. (The attraction between separate water molecules is hydrogen bonding, a much weaker intermolecular force.)

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana

questions.prompt: What is the general molecular formula of alkenes?
questions.workedSolution: Alkenes contain one carbon–carbon double bond and follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ; for n = 2 the compound is ethene, C₂H₄. Alkanes are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ and alkynes CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.

questions.prompt: What is the pH of a 0.001 M solution of hydrochloric acid?
questions.workedSolution: HCl is a strong acid and ionises fully, so [H⁺] = 0.001 = 10⁻³ M. Then pH = −log₁₀[H⁺] = −log₁₀(10⁻³) = 3.

questions.workedSolution: Electrons carry a charge of −1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and occupy the region around the nucleus. Protons are positively charged, neutrons are neutral, and the nucleus as a whole is positive.

questions.prompt: Which type of bond forms when electrons are completely transferred from a metal atom to a non-metal atom?
questions.workedSolution: Complete transfer of electrons produces oppositely charged ions that attract electrostatically — an ionic bond, as in NaCl. Covalent bonding involves sharing, and metallic bonding involves a sea of delocalised electrons.

questions.prompt: In a population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, 9% of individuals show a recessive phenotype. What percentage of the population are heterozygous carriers?
questions.workedSolution: Recessive phenotype frequency q² = 0.09, so q = √0.09 = 0.3. Then p = 1 − q = 0.7. Heterozygote frequency = 2pq = 2 × 0.7 × 0.3 = 0.42, so 42% of the population are carriers.

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana
provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Biology

questions.prompt: A student’s heart beats 72 times per minute with a stroke volume of 75 mL. Calculate the cardiac output in litres per minute.
questions.workedSolution: Cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume = 72 × 75 mL = 5400 mL per minute. Converting to litres: 5400/1000 = 5.4 L/min, a typical resting value for a healthy young adult.

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana
provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Biology

questions.prompt: A DNA molecule contains 30% guanine. What percentage of its bases are adenine?
questions.workedSolution: By Chargaff’s base-pairing rules G = C, so cytosine is also 30% and G + C = 60%. The remaining 40% is shared equally between A and T because A = T, giving adenine = 20%.

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana
provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Biology

questions.prompt: Producers in an ecosystem store 50 000 kJ of energy. If only 10% of energy is transferred between trophic levels, how much energy reaches the secondary consumers?
questions.workedSolution: Each transfer passes on 10%: producers 50 000 kJ → primary consumers 5000 kJ → secondary consumers 500 kJ. The rest is lost mainly as heat through respiration and in undigested material.

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana
provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Biology

questions.prompt: Which pigment captures light energy for photosynthesis?
questions.workedSolution: Chlorophyll, located in the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts, absorbs mainly red and blue light and reflects green, which is why leaves appear green.

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana
provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Biology

questions.prompt: Which blood cells transport oxygen around the body?
questions.workedSolution: Red blood cells (erythrocytes) contain haemoglobin, which binds oxygen in the lungs and releases it in the tissues. They lose their nucleus when mature to carry more haemoglobin.

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana
provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Biology

questions.prompt: What is the basic unit of heredity?
questions.workedSolution: A gene is a section of DNA that codes for a protein (or functional RNA) and is passed from parents to offspring. Genes occur in alternative forms called alleles.

provenance.publisher: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment, Ghana
provenance.title: Secondary Education Curriculum — Biology

questions.prompt: What is the movement of water across a partially permeable membrane called?
questions.workedSolution: Osmosis is the diffusion of water from a region of higher water potential to lower water potential across a partially permeable membrane; it needs no metabolic energy.

questions.prompt: Which vessel returns oxygen-rich blood to the left atrium of the heart?
questions.workedSolution: The pulmonary vein returns oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. The pulmonary artery is unusual in carrying deoxygenated blood (from the heart to the lungs), and the aorta distributes blood from the heart to the body.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme in saliva begins the digestion of starch?
questions.workedSolution: Salivary amylase hydrolyses starch into maltose in the mouth. Pepsin and trypsin digest proteins (in the stomach and small intestine), and lipase digests fats.

questions.prompt: Which product forms in human muscles during anaerobic respiration?
questions.workedSolution: When oxygen supply cannot meet demand, muscles respire anaerobically, converting glucose to lactic acid and releasing a small amount of energy. Ethanol and CO₂ are produced by anaerobic respiration in yeast, not humans.

questions.prompt: To which kingdom do mushrooms belong?
questions.workedSolution: Mushrooms are the fruiting bodies of fungi, which have chitin cell walls, lack chlorophyll and feed by absorbing nutrients from decaying matter. They are neither plants nor animals.
